title: Merge Triplets to Form Target Triplet
pattern: Greedy: use every triplet that cannot overshoot
statement: Merging two triplets takes the **maximum** in each of the three positions. Given `triplets` and a `target` triplet, return `True` if `target` can be obtained by merging some of the triplets (any number of them, in any order).

example.why: Merging [2, 5, 3] and [1, 7, 5] gives [2, 7, 5]. The triplet [1, 8, 4] must be avoided because of its 8.

idea: Merging only ever makes values **larger**. A triplet with any value above the target at that position would push it past the target for good — such a triplet can never be used.
Every other triplet is harmless: all its values are ≤ the target, so merging it in can never overshoot. So simply **merge all harmless triplets**.
If that merged result equals the target, the answer is `True`. Otherwise some target value is not supplied by any usable triplet → `False`.

steps.text: Our example: **`triplets = [[2,5,3],[1,8,4],[1,7,5]], target = [2,7,5]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
`max_values` will be the merge (position-wise maximum) of every triplet we decide to use. Nothing is used yet.
